answer:
Estimate the thermal-mismatch strain in an aluminum film bonded to a ceramic substrate after cooling by ΔT = 180 K (ΔT = −180 K in sign convention, since the film cools).
Use the substrate thermal expansion coefficient α_s = 8×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹.
Use the aluminum film thermal expansion coefficient α_f = 23×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹.
Compute the thermal-mismatch strain as ε = (α_f − α_s) × ΔT_magnitude.
The difference in expansion coefficients is (23×10⁻⁶ − 8×10⁻⁶) = 15×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹.
The mismatch strain is ε = 15×10⁻⁶ × 180 ≈ 2.7×10⁻³.
Report the result as approximately 0.27% tensile strain in the film upon cooling, since the aluminum contracts more than the substrate and ends up in tension.
State the assumption that both film and substrate cool uniformly by 180 K and remain elastically bonded with no interfacial sliding or relaxation.
